flawed_step: Step 4: the claim that some automorphism swaps the two edge-orbit classes X and Y does not follow from regularity plus edge-transitivity.
counterexample: The Folkman-type graph. Take bipartite parts P = the 10 two-element subsets of {1..5} and Q = {i_a : i in {1..5}, a in {1,2}}. Join {i,j} to i_1, i_2, j_1 and j_2. Every vertex has degree 4 (each point lies in 4 pairs), so there are 20 vertices and 40 edges. The group S5 x (Z2)^5 acts transitively on the edges ({i,j}, i_a). Vertices i_1 and i_2 have the same neighbourhood, so each Q-vertex has a twin. Distinct pairs have different neighbourhoods, so no P-vertex has a twin. Automorphisms preserve twins, so the graph is not vertex-transitive.
assessment_summary:
Attempted proof:
1. Let G be regular and edge-transitive, with A = Aut(G). If G has no edges it is empty, and every permutation is an automorphism, so G is vertex-transitive. Justified.
2. Assume G has edges. Every vertex of positive degree lies on an edge, and regularity makes every degree positive. So every vertex is an endpoint of an edge. Since A is transitive on edges, V is the union of the A-orbits of u and v for any fixed edge uv. So A has at most 2 orbits on V. Justified.
3. If there is one orbit we are done. Otherwise the orbits X = A·u and Y = A·v are disjoint. Every edge is an image of uv, so it has one end in X and one in Y. So G is bipartite with parts X and Y, and |X| = |Y| by regularity. Justified.
4. Conclude that some automorphism maps X to Y, making G vertex-transitive. NOT justified: X and Y are orbits of the whole group A, so no automorphism maps a vertex of X into Y. Step 3 only showed that X and Y are separate orbits, and nothing rules that out. Regularity gives |X| = |Y| but no swapping map. This case, called semisymmetric graphs, really occurs.
5. Checking the counterexample (the counterexample field gives the construction): the graph is 4-regular, so it is regular. Justified.
6. S5 acting on the points, together with independently swapping the two copies i_1 and i_2 of each point, gives automorphisms. S5 is transitive on pairs (pair, point in the pair), and the swaps are transitive on the copy index. So the graph is edge-transitive. Justified.
7. Vertices i_1 and i_2 have the same neighbourhood, so Q-vertices have twins. Distinct pairs {i,j} have different neighbourhoods, so P-vertices have no twins. Automorphisms preserve having a twin, so no automorphism maps P to Q, and the graph is not vertex-transitive. Justified.
The general proof fails at step 4, and steps 5–7 give a verified counterexample (this is the Folkman graph). The statement is false.
